SELECTED_INDEX: 4  
CONFIDENCE: 0.35  
EXPLANATION:  
The spectrum shows:  
• Strong C–H stretches at 2930/2964/2997 cm⁻¹ → several alkyl CH₃ groups (Rule GFQ-003).  
• A prominent carbonyl stretch at 1677 cm⁻¹ → amide-type C=O (amide I region).  
• Bands at 1437 and 1390 cm⁻¹ typical of CH₃ asymmetric/symmetric bends and also characteristic of N-nitroso/NO vibrations.  
• Peaks at 1079 cm⁻¹ (N–N stretch of N-nitroso, cf. literature ≈1050–1100 cm⁻¹) and 826 cm⁻¹ (in-plane N=O bending, Rule GFQ-022 range 786–826 cm⁻¹).  
• Band at 603 cm⁻¹ matches amide V / N=O wag (~600 cm⁻¹).  
Among the candidates, only molecule 4 (CN(C)C(=O)N=O) contains
  – an amide carbonyl (C(=O)–) giving the 1677 cm⁻¹ band,
  – an N-nitroso group (–N=O) supplying the 1437, 1079, 826 and 603 cm⁻¹ vibrations,
  – two N-methyl groups providing the strong CH₃ C–H and bending bands.

No other candidate simultaneously offers both an amide carbonyl and an N-nitroso functionality required to account for this specific pattern.
